Code read of apps/api/test/integration/access/sensitive-reach-sweep.test.ts on this candidate. It fills required query parameters from the contract (enums enumerated; ids from seeded rows; the drill-down by every metric and accepted value class, with and without currency and transformationId). It uses each list's maximum limit and follows every nextCursor (readAll). It fails when an admitted control reader (the admitted TL, then the TO) never gets 2xx on a swept request, unless the operation is in ADMITTED_ERROR_ALLOWED: seven entries, each with a stated reason, and the database facts they rely on are asserted (checkJustifications). A stale allowance also fails. Its floor counts operations actually read with 2xx (> 330). Run on this candidate (control, log 54): 555 requests per reader over 371 operations (520 ids), 75 not fillable, 2428 pages read, 364 operations read with 2xx, refused list empty, 2/2 pass. Mutants M1 and M2 (logs 50, 51) show it now catches both round-5 leaks (F-DG6-360, F-DG6-361), which its round-5 version missed. The round-5 instrumented copy (zz-cs-r5-sweep-instrumented) is of the old sweep, so I did not re-run it; the new sweep's own status check replaces it. Residual, judged in my review record (check CS-R6-RESIDUALS): the 75 unfillable operations. The id-routed benefit children among them are guarded by the path-parameter guard (route parameter names checked against SENSITIVE_REACH_PARAMS). The sweep judges only titles and values, not identifiers, which is new finding F-DG6-420, a different defect class than this one.
